sections.h2: What does a Florida quitclaim deed actually do?
sections.html:
A Florida quitclaim deed hands over whatever interest the signer holds in a parcel, with no promise that the interest is good or that the title is clean. The buyer or relative receiving it takes the same position the signer was in, defects included.

Because of that, owners most often use a quitclaim deed between people who already trust each other: adding a spouse, moving a house into a family trust, or removing a name after a divorce. Sellers dealing with strangers usually find that a buyer, lender or title insurer asks for a warranty deed or a special warranty deed, since those carry some assurance about title.

The deed still has to be a proper Florida conveyance. Nothing about the word "quitclaim" lowers the formalities, the recording rules or the tax.

sections.h2: How must a quitclaim deed be signed and witnessed in Florida?
sections.html:
Florida law requires the deed to be in writing and signed in front of two subscribing witnesses, and no seal is needed (s. 689.01). The statute also allows the witnessing to happen through audio-video technology.

Recording adds a second layer of requirements. Under s. 695.26 the clerk of the circuit court may not record the instrument unless it shows:

  • the printed name of every person who signed, with a post-office address for each;
  • the name and post-office address of the natural person who prepared the deed;
  • the printed name and address of each witness, plus the name of any notary under the notary's signature;
  • a 3-inch by 3-inch blank space at the top right of the first page and a 1-inch by 3-inch space on each later page, kept clear for the clerk;
  • the grantee's name and post-office address.

A deed signed outside Florida is among the instruments the section does not apply to, and a clerk who records a deed that misses a step does not undo the recording. Even so, a deed that fails these checks is the one most likely to be bounced at the counter, so check each item before you drive to the clerk.

sections.h2: Is documentary stamp tax due on a quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
Yes. The Department of Revenue lists quit claim deeds among the taxable deeds, alongside warranty, special warranty, trustee's and life estate deeds, and the statute puts the rate at 70 cents on each $100 of consideration (s. 201.02).

Consideration is broader than cash. The statute counts money paid, any obligation discharged, and any mortgage or encumbrance on the parcel, whether or not the new owner assumes it. A "gift" of a house with a loan on it can therefore still carry a taxable base.

The Department of Revenue states that all parties to the document are liable for the tax, whoever agrees to pay it, and that if one party is exempt a non-exempt party must pay. The county clerk collects the tax when the deed is recorded, and the department collects it when a taxable deed is never recorded (DOR documentary stamp tax page).

The department also says there is no specific exemption for transferring Florida real property for estate planning. Moving your own house into a revocable trust by quitclaim deed is therefore not automatically free of tax. Ask the clerk or a Florida attorney how the rule applies to your facts before you sign.

sections.h2: Which quitclaim transfers are exempt, and what do the fees look like?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue describes two exempt situations: a spousal homestead deed where the only consideration is a mortgage, and a deed for the marital home delivered in a divorce (s. 201.02(7)). A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable as well.

Recording itself costs money too. The clerk's fee schedule in s. 28.24 is summarized below.

Clerk chargeAmount printed in s. 28.24(13)
First page$5.00
Each additional page$4.00
Each name beyond four$1.00
Modernization trust fund charge$1.00 first page, $0.50 each additional page
Technology charge$4 per page, added on top

Source: Florida Statutes, s. 28.24. Ask the clerk in your county for the total on a specific deed, since the page count and the number of names change it.

sections.h2: Does a quitclaim deed change the property tax bill?
sections.html:
It can. Florida treats any sale, foreclosure or other transfer of legal or beneficial title as a change of ownership, which resets the assessed value to just value the next January 1 unless an exception applies (DOR Save Our Homes guidance).

The statute lists exceptions, among them transfers where the same person stays entitled to the benefit, transfers between spouses, and corrective deeds (s. 193.155). A long-held homestead with a low assessed value is the house where an unplanned reset hurts most.

Homestead status is a separate question. A homestead exemption is filed on Form DR-501 with the county property appraiser by March 1, and the owner must have made the home the permanent residence by January 1. Check with the property appraiser before deeding a homestead to anyone.

sections.h2: When is a quitclaim deed the wrong tool for selling a Florida house?
sections.html:
It is the wrong tool whenever the buyer is paying real money and wants protection. A quitclaim deed gives the buyer no warranty, and a title company will often decline to insure a sale that depends on one.

Common situations where owners reach for a quitclaim deed and then run into trouble:

  • Several heirs hold the house and one of them signs alone. A quitclaim passes only that one heir's share.
  • A mortgage is still on the property. The deed does not remove the loan, and the lender is not bound by the transfer.
  • A relative is added to the deed to avoid probate. The transfer is immediate, so the relative becomes a co-owner whose signature is needed to sell.
  • The owner wants to keep control during life. A different instrument, the enhanced life estate deed, is built for that.

On that last point, a Department of Revenue advisement (TAA 20B4-004, October 2020) concluded that a lady bird deed in the situation described did not transfer a present beneficial interest and so was not subject to documentary stamp tax. That conclusion rested on the facts presented, so confirm how it applies to yours.

sections.h2: How can an owner sell a Florida house when the title is messy?
sections.html:
Start by finding out who legally owns the house, then fix gaps in the chain with the right instrument. A quitclaim deed can clear a name from title when that person agrees, but it cannot create ownership that nobody held.

If the problem is an inherited house with several heirs, the probate court usually has to authorize the transfer. If the problem is back taxes or a lien, the payoff has to come out of the sale. A buyer who purchases as-is for cash can work around repairs and clutter, though not around a missing signature.

Bring the deeds, any mortgage statement, the property tax bill and a list of every person who may hold an interest. With those papers a title company can tell you quickly what is needed to close.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to record a Florida quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: No law in the pages reviewed requires a lawyer for signing, but the deed must meet the two-witness rule and the recording checklist in ss. 689.01 and 695.26. Because tax and title consequences follow, many owners have a Florida attorney or title company prepare it.

faqs.q: Who pays the doc stamps on a quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: All parties to the document are liable under the Department of Revenue's description, whichever party agrees to pay. The clerk collects the tax when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What is the doc stamp rate on a Florida deed?
faqs.a: The statute sets 70 cents on each $100 of consideration. The Department of Revenue notes Miami-Dade County has its own rate and a surtax that does not apply to a document transferring only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: Can a quitclaim deed change my homestead assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. A transfer of title counts as a change of ownership unless an exception in s. 193.155 applies, and the property resets to just value the following January 1.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed the same as a lady bird deed?
faqs.a: No. A quitclaim deed passes the signer's interest now, while a lady bird deed keeps life-time control with the owner. The Department of Revenue advisement on lady bird deeds turned on the powers the life tenants kept.
